rules.sentence: The diagnosis is suggested by characteristic neurologic deficits and by back pain worsened by recumbency, particularly in patients who have a fever or have had a recent infection.
Diagnosis is by MRI; myelography followed by CT can be used if MRI is not available.

Antibiotics with or without parenteral needle aspiration may be sufficient; however, abscesses causing neurologic compromise (eg, paresis, bowel or bladder dysfunction) are surgically drained immediately.
Pending culture results, antibiotics to cover staphylococcus and anaerobes are given as for brain abscess (.
If the abscess developed after a neurosurgical procedure, an aminoglycoside is added to cover gram-negative bacteria.

Spinal subdural or epidural hematoma (usually thoracic or lumbar) is rare but may result from back trauma, anticoagulant or thrombolytic therapy, or, in patients with bleeding diatheses, lumbar puncture.
Symptoms begin with local or radicular back pain and percussion tenderness; they are often severe.
Spinal cord compression may develop; compression of lumbar spinal roots may cause cauda equina syndrome and lower extremity paresis.
